column4: When humanity is gathered, the beings they worshipped become their enemies and deny that worship, so the assembly exposes earthly relations.
The day is defined as the time when all people stand before the Lord of all worlds, a direct universal presence before their Lord.
Solomon's forces of jinn, humans, and birds are mustered and held in ordered ranks, a concrete royal and military gathering on the smaller scale.
The people who turned back on the day the two hosts met locate moral failure inside the same battlefield meeting of gathered crowds.
What struck the believers on the day the two hosts met occurred by God's permission, another exact battlefield use of the gathered-crowd formula.
The opponents appear gathered together while their hearts are scattered, directly opposing an outward crowd to the divided contents that lie within breasts.
The trumpet-day belongs to the knower of the unseen and the witnessed, joining resurrection's summons to the boundary between hidden and manifest.
The trumpet is blown and the ayah identifies this as the promised day, opening the sequence in which every soul arrives with driver and witness.
When the trumpet is blown, kinship no longer operates and people do not question one another, dissolving ordinary crowd-relations inside the final muster.
The trumpet terrifies everyone in heavens and earth except those God wills, and all come to Him humbled, combining universal summons with an explicit exception.
A caller summons people to something dreadful; this is the initiating voice toward which the grave-crowd of 54:7-8 emerges and hurries.
On that day everyone follows the caller without deviation and voices fall quiet, giving the gathered sinners of 20:102 one direction and subdued collective sound.
Humbled eyes and enveloping abasement identify the grave-rush of 70:43 as the very day the crowd had been promised.
The Day of Decision is an appointed time, supplying the fixed communal appointment whose trumpet and arriving crowds appear in 78:18.
A single blast on the trumpet begins this judgment sequence, another direct formulation of one sound initiating the final event.
After the single trumpet blast and cosmic crushing, this ayah says that on that day the Event occurs, identifying the sounding's result.
The people suddenly raised by the one cry recognize their woe and name what has overtaken them as the Day of Recompense.
The answer identifies the crowd's recognized day as the Day of Decision they had denied, stating the purpose of their sudden collective presence.
Whether people disclose or conceal what is within themselves, God calls them to account for it, closely matching the collected contents of breasts.
When graves are overturned and emptied, the bodily containers release their contents immediately before each soul knows its moral contents in 82:5.
After the graves are overturned, every soul knows what it sent ahead and left behind, paralleling the disclosure produced by collecting what breasts contain.
Each person's deed-record is fastened to them and brought out on Resurrection as an open book, making a hidden moral total present for the self-reading of 17:14.
On that day the human is informed of what he sent ahead and left behind, an explicit disclosure of the completed contents of his life.
The veil is removed and sight becomes sharp, describing the new exposure of the soul that has just arrived with its driver and witness.
The magicians are told to collect their whole scheme and then come in one row, joining gathered intention to an ordered public company.
Pharaoh sends musterers through the cities, initiating the collection of the pursuing force whose two crowds finally see each other in 26:61.
The mustered force pursues at sunrise, supplying both the morning movement and the approaching crowd immediately before the two hosts see one another.
A single cry seizes people while they are disputing, a death-summons that contrasts with the later single cry making everyone present before God.
Although God has counted them all, every one comes to Him individually on Resurrection, preserving individual exposure inside the universal gathering.
Everyone in heavens and earth comes to the Merciful as a servant, defining the common status of the persons counted in 19:94.
God has comprehended and counted every one of them exactly, giving the universal multitude an exhaustive individual accounting before 19:95.
The people dispersed to see their deeds in 99:6 each see even an atom's weight of good, specifying the disclosed contents of that day.
Each also sees an atom's weight of evil, completing the minute disclosure for the dispersed people of 99:6.
Pharaoh's counselors tell him to send gatherers through the cities, a direct human mechanism for producing the public crowd of magicians.
The same counsel orders city-gatherers to be dispatched, a repeated worldly use of commissioned agents who assemble a crowd for confrontation.
Pharaoh's people describe themselves as a wholly alert company after the muster, characterizing the pursuing crowd before its sunrise advance.
The trumpet is sounded, introducing the difficult day named in 74:9 and repeating the audible trigger of the gathering.
The trumpet sounding of 74:8 is identified as a difficult day, giving the summons its temporal and judgmental character.
God knows what the human self whispers and is nearer than the jugular vein, defining the prior divine knowledge of the contents later exposed.
The question whether God best knows what lies in all people's breasts makes inward content a universally known field rather than a private secret.
Jesus will be a witness against the People of the Book on Resurrection, assigning a named witness to a particular community in the assembly.
The Messenger is sent as a witness over the addressed people, giving the section's witness a communal speaker-addressee relation like Moses before Pharaoh.
God addresses the Prophet as a witness among his commissioned roles, identifying who bears testimony over the community brought to judgment.
The repeated commissioning sends the Prophet as witness, bearer of good news, and warner, connecting present proclamation to later testimony.
The queen says she decides no affair until her counselors are present with her, a council scene using witnessing in the developed sense of attendance.
Had the disrupters joined the army, they would have rushed through its midst seeking discord, a specific internal penetration of a gathered force.
Divine force reaches a settlement by night or during its midday rest, a nonlexical parallel to a community being caught by a sudden incursion.
All disputants contend before their Lord on Resurrection, turning common presence with the Lord into an adjudicated confrontation.
Noah challenges his people to collect their plan and partners before acting against him, applying gathering to a hostile coalition and its settled purpose.
Successive communities enter the Fire until all have joined one another there, making a final collected company whose members curse each other.
The command to hold fast all together and not divide makes human gathering an ethical unity explicitly bounded by dispersal.
Those implicated in the claimed kinship with the jinn know they will be brought into compulsory presence, another eschatological use of attendance.
Humanity and jinn are imagined assembling for one shared task yet remaining collectively unable, a bounded use of the largest creaturely crowd.
The community is told to mobilize in separate groups or all together, a military contrast between smaller companies and one massed force.
